speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Half the parish is on the stair, and the mayor who does not live among us is the one in the barge. Keep your footing.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I am keeping it, mistress. The weed is green on the lower step.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: Hold where you are, Master Will. I am on the oars, and I am not making a wherry of a show.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not hiring you, Davy. I am looking.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: New Mayor! He'll pull down the playhouses by Christmas, the old one's to be an earl, and the Spaniard's in the Downs.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have three news and one tide. I am not buying the news.

speaker: (the passenger)
text: Take me after the barge. Put me under their streamers as far as the bridge.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: Follow it in your own boat, or swim. The oars are not stopping for a fare.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is the line I am keeping. The rest of the river can shout.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You are very choice for a man on a wet step. I came down for the drums, and the drums are worth the weed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You may have the drums. I am not in a hat for this.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Farewell, thy sour worship. Go sweeten.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: He took his hat off toward Bishopsgate. I hope the hat knows whom it means. The man in the barge does not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The hat is for the one who is going out. I am not bowing with it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Sir John is at the back of his own company, sir. He is not looking at the stair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I am not looking for a word from him. He never gave me one.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The sword has gone before another man. He went out as he came in, liking nobody. Well. He kept his own door.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He kept it. This is not a victory for anyone on these steps. The next man will have the same letters to write.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: The oarsmen are what keeps the barge a barge. The marshals and their staves keep the street from sitting down in the river. You may enjoy that, if you will not enjoy a mayor.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is the part I am enjoying. The labour of it. Mistress Ansell may have the order.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I will have the order. It is the first time this year the sword has told the truth about who walks first.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is a woman at the edge of the crowd, mistress. Dark head. She is turned away, and she is laughing.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I see the head. I am not looking long enough to know who stands beside her.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then do not. A laugh on a stair is not a name, and I will not have you collect one.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You can leave a laugh where it is. I am for the yard at two, if the drums finish. You are in the old play, I hear.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am in it. Egeon, at both ends. I am not sitting down between a barge and a play.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: Then go up dry, Master Will. This was not a hire.

speaker: (the passenger)
text: I will find another boat.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: Find it. Or swim. I have said which.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: We are going up. Alse, the parish will still be here when we are not. Do not stay to be civil to a crowd.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I am behind you, mistress.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Up. I have one line to put on the tables, and then the lane.
